subtype: Approach: trying and falling and trying again [Action]
passage: At the community centre ground, Nirmal held the handlebars of a small red cycle. No training wheels, only Damini the coach nearby with folded arms. "Ready?" Nirmal pushed off, wobbled twice and toppled onto the grass. Up again. This time he went four pedals before the front wheel twisted. Again. Six pedals. Damini said nothing but nodded. After an hour his knees were scuffed and his shirt was green with grass, but he was smiling. "I think I felt it," he said. "The falling part isn't so scary now." The last try took him almost to the far fence.

qa.q: How many pedals did Nirmal manage on the second try?
What might Nirmal feel when saying the falling part is not so scary?
qa.a: Nirmal probably feels growing confidence and a little pride, because the scuffed knees did not stop the smile. 😊

qa.q: What alternative approach could Nirmal use to learn faster, and why?
qa.a: Nirmal could ask Damini to hold the seat for the first pedals or glide without pedals first. That would give balance practice with less fear.

qa.q: How might Damini see Nirmal's tries?
qa.a: Damini stood with folded arms and only nodded, so Damini seems to trust the practice and probably sees steady improvement.

grounding: A boy hops on a cycle without training wheels, wobbles and falls, and each try lets him balance a little longer while fear fades.
